stories.category: Pakistan Foreign Policy, UNGA & Regional Security
stories.headline: Shehbaz Sharif uses UNGA-81 address to set out Pakistan's positions on water security, Afghanistan, Palestine and climate finance
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the 81st UN General Assembly that Pakistan regards the Indus Waters Treaty as valid and operative, demanded verifiable Afghan action against militant sanctuaries, called for open maritime chokepoints, stronger climate finance and a representative UN Security Council.
stories.what_happened: In his 26 September address in New York, the Prime Minister linked South Asian stability to Kashmir and water security, described the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab as arteries of the global economy, urged action against militants using Afghan territory, and called for debt relief, affordable development finance and faster loss-and-damage support.
stories.background: The address came during UNGA-81 amid heightened Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions, regional maritime disruption and Pakistan's continuing dispute with India over the Indus Waters Treaty.
stories.why_it_matters: The speech consolidates Pakistan's current diplomatic positions across security, water, development finance, climate justice and UN reform in one high-level policy statement.
stories.pakistan_perspective: For Pakistan, water security, cross-border militancy and climate vulnerability are framed as international-law and collective-security questions rather than solely bilateral issues.
stories.regional_implications: Pakistan's warning against interference with its water share and its demand for Afghan action against militant sanctuaries underline two major sources of South Asian instability.
stories.global_implications: The call to keep Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab open connects Pakistan's diplomacy directly to global energy and trade security.
key_takeaways: Pakistan said the Indus Waters Treaty remains valid, binding and fully operative.
The Prime Minister said attempts to stop, impede or divert Pakistan's share of water would be treated as an act of war.
Pakistan called on Afghan authorities to take verifiable and decisive action so Afghan soil is not used against Pakistan or any other country.
Pakistan called for timely debt relief, affordable long-term financing, climate finance and faster loss-and-damage support.
Pakistan reiterated support for a Palestinian state on pre-1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.

stories.headline: President approves Islamabad Safe City surveillance-protection ordinance
stories.summary: President Asif Ali Zardari approved an ordinance protecting Islamabad Safe City cameras and surveillance infrastructure and creating a compensation and appeal mechanism for damage.
stories.what_happened: The Islamabad Capital Territory Safe City Camera and Surveillance Infrastructure Protection and Damage Compensation Ordinance permits financial penalties for damaging or encouraging damage to surveillance infrastructure and can hold organisers responsible for damage during rallies, processions, sit-ins, protests, strikes or gatherings.
stories.why_it_matters: The measure directly intersects public-order management, surveillance infrastructure, protest organisation and procedural rights in the federal capital.
key_takeaways: The President approved the ordinance on the Prime Minister's advice.
An authorised officer determines fines and damage costs after an opportunity of hearing.
A person can appeal the determination before the District and Sessions Judge, Islamabad, within 30 days.
what_to_watch: Implementation rules and enforcement during public gatherings
Any constitutional or judicial challenge to organiser liability
question_angles: Public-order regulation and procedural safeguards in Islamabad

stories.headline: Pakistan raises petrol to Rs391.30 per litre while cutting high-speed diesel to Rs408.53
stories.summary: The Petroleum Division revised fuel prices for 26 September, increasing petrol by Rs2.02 per litre and reducing high-speed diesel by Rs3.59 per litre.
stories.why_it_matters: Fuel-price movements feed directly into household costs, freight, inflation expectations and fiscal management.
key_takeaways: Petrol rose by Rs2.02 per litre to Rs391.30.
High-speed diesel fell by Rs3.59 per litre to Rs408.53.
what_to_watch: Pass-through to transport and food prices
Further revisions under the current petroleum pricing mechanism
question_angles: Petroleum pricing and inflation transmission in Pakistan

stories.category: United Nations, Nuclear Disarmament & Strategic Stability
stories.headline: UN marks International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons amid modernisation of global arsenals
stories.summary: The United Nations observed the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons on 26 September, while the General Assembly scheduled its 2026 high-level commemorative plenary for 29 September because the observance fell on a Saturday.
stories.background: The General Assembly established the observance through resolution 68/32. The UN says nuclear disarmament remains its highest disarmament priority and notes that more than 12,000 nuclear weapons remain worldwide.
stories.why_it_matters: The observance keeps nuclear-risk reduction, deterrence doctrines, arms modernisation and disarmament diplomacy on the multilateral agenda at a time of heightened geopolitical competition.
key_takeaways: The International Day is observed annually on 26 September.
The 2026 high-level General Assembly plenary is scheduled for 29 September.
The UN General Assembly established the observance through resolution 68/32.
UN material for the event says more than 12,000 nuclear weapons remain.

stories.headline: Moldova's 60-day energy and water state of emergency takes effect
stories.summary: A 60-day state of emergency approved by Moldova's parliament to secure energy and water supplies took effect on 26 September.
stories.background: Parliament approved the measure on 22 September by 54 votes to 20, with 22 abstentions, giving the government additional authority to respond rapidly to supply risks.
stories.why_it_matters: Moldova's exposure to regional energy disruption illustrates the security dimension of essential-service resilience for states bordering the Ukraine war zone.
stories.regional_implications: The emergency highlights continuing energy-security vulnerabilities in Eastern Europe and Moldova's need to protect critical supply systems.
key_takeaways: The emergency took effect on 26 September and lasts 60 days.
Moldova's parliament approved it by 54 votes to 20, with 22 abstentions.
The measure focuses on energy and water supply security.
